answer:
LoRA learns an additive low-rank matrix update; it can usually be merged into a compatible dense weight for inference. DoRA separates weight magnitude from direction, applying low-rank adaptation to the direction with a separately learned magnitude. Prefix tuning learns continuous prefix states that attention can consult. Bottleneck adapters insert trainable down-projection, nonlinearity, and up-projection modules between frozen layers. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09353) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.00190)

$$\Delta W_{LoRA}=BA,\qquad W_{DoRA}=m\frac{W_0+BA}{\|W_0+BA\|}\ \text{along the chosen weight axis}.$$

Prefix tuning increases attention/cache work; unmerged adapters add computation; merged LoRA avoids its extra matrix operations but requires storing or materializing a merged model. Compare trainable parameter count, activation memory, task quality, switching latency, and multi-adapter serving—not just checkpoint size.
